title: GH#7633: Fix anthropic/ prefix for Anthropic models in OpenCode tier config
body:
## Summary

- Fixes `model-availability-helper.sh resolve opus` returning `opencode/claude-opus-4-6` instead of `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`
- OpenCode uses `anthropic/` as the provider prefix for all Anthropic models — `opencode/claude-*` causes `ProviderModelNotFoundError` at dispatch time
- Applies the same fix to all affected tiers: `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `coding`, `health`, `eval`

## Root Cause

`get_tier_models()` had an OpenCode-available branch that used `opencode/claude-*` model IDs for Anthropic models. OpenCode's gateway routes Anthropic models under the `anthropic/` provider prefix, not `opencode/`. Non-Anthropic models (`gemini-*`, `gpt-*`) correctly retain their `opencode/` prefix.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh`: Replace `opencode/claude-*` → `anthropic/claude-*` in the OpenCode branch of `get_tier_models()`. Updated comment to document the correct prefix convention.
- `tests/test-model-availability.sh`: Add regression tests (GH#7633 block) asserting no tier returns an `opencode/claude-*` model ID.

## Testing

- `bash -n` syntax check: PASS
- `shellcheck`: PASS (0 errors)
- New GH#7633 regression tests: 6/6 PASS
- Full test suite: 28 pass, 5 fail (same 5 pre-existing failures on main — supervisor-helper.sh not present, help text check)
- Tier resolution table verified: `opus` → `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`, `coding` → `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk**: Low — config-only change, no logic change
- **Testing level**: self-assessed
- **Behaviour verified**: `model-availability-helper.sh status` tier table shows correct `anthropic/` prefixes for all Anthropic model tiers

Closes #7633
